claims.claim: The sunlight on your skin is a hundred thousand years old.
claims.note: Fails A4: a viewer who swipes after this sentence leaves believing the light is 100,000 years old, which is the popular false version the script itself corrects ('The light is eight minutes old'). Also A3: Mitalas & Sills abstract gives 170,000 yr; bare 'a hundred thousand' with no 'about' goes past the A3 outer limit. And the energy reading is disputed: Stix's abstract (read at publisher) puts the energy-transport time at the Kelvin-Helmholtz scale, ~3e7 yr, ~100x the photon diffusion time. Change to a hook true under both sources, e.g. 'The energy in the sunlight on your skin spent more than a hundred thousand years getting out of the Sun.' ('more than' holds for 1.7e5 and for 3e7).

claims.claim: Eight minutes of that was the trip from the Sun.
claims.source_checked: IAU 2012 Resolution B2 (English PDF linked from https://www.iau.org/IAU/Iau/Publications/List-of-Resolutions.aspx: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1FBKjaswlP-rTs6z6V4WygXsbdHKVHYcP/view); https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/cuu/Value?c (CODATA 2022)
claims.note: AU = 149 597 870 700 m exactly (IAU 2012 B2); c = 299 792 458 m/s exact (NIST). 1 AU / c = 499.0 s = 8 min 19 s; 'eight minutes' is fair rounding (Earth-Sun distance varies ~±1.7%, 8.2-8.5 min). SOURCES entry 1 should name IAU 2012 B2 and CODATA as the sources of the two constants (A1).
Same arithmetic as claim 2: photosphere to Earth ~499 s.

In context this says the energy took ~100,000 years to get out. Mitalas & Sills' 170,000 yr is a photon random-walk time; Stix (publisher abstract) says the time scale of energy transport is ~3e7 yr. The sentence is only safe once the hook says 'more than a hundred thousand years' (claim 1 fix); keep it but make the number it refers to a lower bound.

Mitalas & Sills: 170,000 yr photon diffusion time scale; ≈100,000 is at A3's rounding limit. But the script says no photon makes the trip, so the only thing going core to surface is energy, which Stix puts at ~3e7 yr. Change to '100,000+ YEARS' (or '>100,000 YEARS') / 'core to surface', matching the spoken fix; alternatively '≈170,000 YEARS' explicitly labelled as the photon random-walk estimate.

This is exactly the gloss Stix's abstract rejects: 'the time scale of energy transport in the Sun is the Kelvin-Helmholtz time scale, of order 3x10^7 years, roughly 100 times longer than the photon-diffusion time estimated by Mitalas and Sills'. Change to 'THE ENERGY / 100,000+ years getting out' (true under both sources). Also update SOURCES entry 2: Stix was now read at the publisher (abstract), figure is ~3e7 yr, so the range is 1.7e5 to ~3e7, not ~1.7e7.

claims.claim: But it is not the same light. No photon survives the climb.
claims.source_checked: https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml (NASA Marshall, The Solar Interior); https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084 (NASA SVS, Origin of Light)
claims.note: Substance is supported: NASA SVS says photons are 'absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly' on the way out; NASA MSFC says energy crosses the radiative zone as radiation (mostly gamma- and X-rays) and the outer ~30% by convective fluid flows, then 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light', so no core photon can reach the surface. But SOURCES entry 4 cites no source at all (A1/A2). Add a citation, e.g. the NASA MSFC page above or a textbook with edition (e.g. Stix, The Sun: An Introduction, 2nd ed., Springer 2002). The '~1 MeV / ~2 eV ~ a million photons' line in entry 4 is unsourced order-of-magnitude reasoning; cite or drop it (not spoken).
True under either reading: 1.7e5 yr (Mitalas & Sills) or ~3e7 yr (Stix).

claims.claim: The light is eight minutes old.
claims.note: Light leaving the photosphere reaches Earth in ~499 s (claim 2); NASA SVS: 'Light takes eight minutes to travel ... from the sun to Earth'.

claims.claim: Radiative zone extends to 0.7 solar radii; convective zone from there to the surface; energy originates in the core (fusion within ~0.25 R)
claims.note: Helioseismic convection-zone depth 0.287 ± 0.003 R, i.e. base at 0.713 R. NASA MSFC: core innermost 25%, radiative zone 25%-70%, convection zone outermost 30%. SOURCES entry 6 says only 'standard solar model figures'; add the Christensen-Dalsgaard et al. 1991 citation (A1). Temperatures in entry 6 (15.7 MK, 5,772 K) were not listed as on-screen; 5,772 K matches IAU 2015 Resolution B3 (Teff = 5772.0 ± 0.8 K).

claims.claim: One photon path random-walks out of the core through the radiative zone, then breaks out quickly through the convective zone
claims.note: A6: the visual shows a single photon making the whole trip, contradicting the spoken 'No photon survives the climb', and shows photon travel through the convection zone, where NASA MSFC says energy is carried by convective fluid flows, not radiation. 'Quickly' itself is supported ('convective motions carry heat quite rapidly to the surface'); the 'weeks to months' figure in SOURCES entry 3 is uncited. Change: show the path handing off (e.g. the dot changes colour/wavelength at absorptions, or label it 'energy, not one photon'), switch to rising convection cells above 0.7 R, and add an on-screen 'not to scale' (a 0.09 cm step across 700,000 km cannot be drawn to scale).
